name: Thomas James
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Thomas James inherited and grew his fortune through financial services business Raymond James, which was started by his father, Robert, in 1962.
He stepped down as Raymond James' chairman in 2017, having served for over 40 years.
He retired from the company's board of directors in February 2024.
He is an avid art collector. Part of his collection is on display at the James Museum of Western & Wildlife Art.
He is a graduate of Harvard College and Harvard Business School.
forbes_facts: James and his wife began collecting art while both were still students.

name: James Packer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: James Packer was the largest shareholder of Crown Resorts, which owns casinos in Australia and London. He took over the empire of his late father, Kerry.
Packer stepped down from Crown Resorts' board in March 2018. Four months later, he resigned from the board of his family company, Consolidated Press.
Packer's board exits were reportedly due to mental health issues, following a tough year when Crown exited its Macau and U.S. gambling investments.
Packer settled with his older sister Gretel in 2015, agreeing to a division of assets 10 years after their late father's death.
Packer has teamed up with American actor Robert De Niro to build a $500 million resort in Barbuda, aiming to open in early 2026.
forbes_facts: Packer was briefly engaged to American singer Mariah Carey but he broke off the engagement and reportedly had to pay her a settlement.
Packer spends much time lately at his Ellerstina polo ranch in Argentina. He also shares a house in Aspen with his ex-wife Erica Baxter with whom he has three kids.
In May 2023, Packer and the Packer Family Foundation gave $4.5 million to support mental health research at UNSW Sydney.

name: Luca Querella
forbes_bio: Luca Querella cofounded Italian app developer Bending Spoons in 2013 with his three cofounders Luca Ferrari, Matteo Danieli and Francesco Patarnello.
The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

name: Bernard Lewis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Bernard Lewis founded UK-based clothing retailer River Island Fashion in 1948; it now sells online and has stores in several European countries.
The business had revenues in 2022 of over $900 million.
His nephew Ben Lewis, who started as a store manager in 1990, serves as CEO.
Lewis and his family are also investors in property development and private equity across UK, Europe, US, Caribbean and Thailand.
forbes_facts: Lewis launched his entrepreneurial career at age 20 by establishing a fruit & vegetable stall in a makeshift shack constructed on a bombsite in North London in 1946.
In 2025, River Island faced severe financial pressures, prompting a restructuring plan to avert bankruptcy.

name: Chen Ailian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2004-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017)
forbes_bio: Chen Ailian chairs Zhejiang Wanfeng Auto Wheel, a supplier of aluminum alloy wheels for automobiles.
Chen is the wife of former billionaire Wu Liangding, who founded Wanfeng Auto Holdings Group.
Its customers include BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Land Rover, GM, Ford, Volkswagen, Toyota, Honda, Nissan and Hyundai, among others.
In 1994, Chen founded an aluminum wheel factory in Shaoxing, in Zhejiang province, the predecessor of Wanfeng Auto Holding Group.
She led Wanfeng's acquisitions of Meridian in Canada, Paslin in the U.S. and a Canadian aircraft manufacturing project.

name: Alicia Koplowitz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: In the early 1960s, Alicia Koplowitz inherited a stake in Spanish construction company Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas after her father died.
She sold her stake to sister Esther for $800 million in 1997 and put the money into diverse investments.
Over the years she's invested in steelmaker Acerinox, electric utility Iberdrola, and Banco Sabadell.
Koplowitz owns hotels in Italy and Miami, real estate in Washington, D.C. and Chicago, as well as a stake in Hospes, a Spanish luxury hotel chain.
Her charitable foundation sends Spanish fellows to study child psychiatry in England and the U.S. at Columbia University, Stanford and others.
forbes_facts: In 1969 when she was a teenager she married Alberto Cortina, six months after her sister Esther married Cortina's cousin, Alberto Alcocer.
Koplowitz owns property in Madrid with Amancio Ortega, the Spanish billionaire known for fashion giant Zara.

name: Simon Nixon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (18)
forbes_bio: Simon Nixon earned the bulk of his fortune from his price-comparison website MoneySuperMarket.
He cofounded the company in 1993, took it public in 2007, and sold all his shares in it by 2016.
Nixon has invested in dozens of private companies, including--before they went public--Airbnb, Robinhood and Wise (formerly called Transferwise).
He also owns luxury homes around the globe, including in Malibu and Barbados, which he lists for private holiday rentals on his site, SimonEscapes.
forbes_facts: In 2013, Nixon moved from Chester, England, to tax haven Jersey, where he owns a multi-million dollar home.
Nixon studied accounting at Nottingham University before dropping out at the age of 20.

name: Sam Goi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Son of a Fujian farmer, Sam Goi owns Tee Yih Jia Food Manufacturing, one of the world's largest makers of popiah skins, which are used for spring rolls.
After completing secondary school education, he joined his father's grocery business. He later ventured into the frozen food industry by acquiring a struggling food business,
He also has real estate interests through his stakes in listed firms GSH and KOP.
In 2021, he became chairman of Singapore-based consumer goods firm Hanwell Industries after a boardroom tussle. Hanwell is now PSC where he owns a majority stake.
Goi is Singapore's non-resident ambassador to Brazil.
forbes_facts: Goi sold a 28-story office tower in Singapore for $512 million to a Chinese buyer in 2017.
He collects both local and Chinese artworks and antiques.
Goi built a new factory in Singapore for S$450 mill, which opened in 2023.
